A1.justification: Despite the changed title and SeMem-to-MoNIM reframing, the PDFs share the underlying selective-memory approach and extensive matching experiments. Both contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original continual-learning experiments, language-modeling and downstream-task results, and memorization and calibrator ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations, baseline comparisons, selection ablations and inference-timing results.

M1.justification: The frozen-LM, kNN memory and neural-calibrator pipeline remains. V2 adds an adaptive memorization threshold, an alternative KL-based selector and optional confidence-based retrieval skipping (Section 3.2; Appendices C.1 and C.6). These refine the procedure; the FFN-bypass interpretation alone does not establish an implemented architectural replacement.

E1.justification: V2 adds News Crawl articles from the first week of October 2024 for the Llama-3.2 evaluation. The earlier news periods, WikiEvent, Wiki-103, ACL papers, REALTIME QA and general NLP tasks remain; shortened dataset names do not represent additional coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Greedy Merging to the continual-learning comparison in Table 5 and FullMem to the ACL domain-adaptation comparison in Table 6. Existing comparators remain in their corresponding experiments, including fine-tuning, RecAdam, MixReview and RandMem.

E3.justification: V2 extends model-scaling evaluation to Llama-3.2 1B and 3B and adds relative-latency evaluation, including retrieval skipping at threshold 0.3. The original chronological news evaluation, held-out proportions, daily index updates and four-batch ACL procedure remain. These are added configurations and procedures, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds comparisons of loss-based versus KL-based selection, memorization with versus without AMT, and inference-time versus perplexity trade-offs. These investigate additional selection, compression and computational-cost questions. The earlier threshold, calibrator and in-context-learning analyses are retained after relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions select the best-performing RandMem run from three random-seed runs. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates; forgetting differences in parentheses are performance changes, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: With AMT introduced, reported GPT-2 memory rates change from 53/48/42% to 50/46/40%, while corresponding perplexities remain 8.6/7.2/6.3. Large-model next-word accuracy changes from 48.7 to 48.5. V2 adds Llama, Greedy Merging, ACL FullMem, KL-selection and timing results. Its main QA table changes 36.3 to 36.2, although appendix Table 16 retains 36.3.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2.3 adds FFN and attention-update decompositions, a near-linearity assumption for layer normalization, a definition of an ideal local concept mixture, and a log-space interpolation derivation. This mathematical account of memory as an FFN-like bypass is absent from v1's kNN and threshold formulation.

C1.justification: V1's central contribution is selective memorization for scalable continual learning. V2 retains the scalability claim but adds a central claim that MoNIM integrates induction-head capabilities and FFN-style concept promotion into a learnable memory framework. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion substantially redefine the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving local induction versus global reasoning, AMT reducing memory overfitting, and distribution shifts caused by greedy merging or noisy FullMem retrieval. Its new Limitations section explicitly restricts the framework to kNN-LM and acknowledges unaddressed architectures, limited temporal coverage and evaluation only up to 3B parameters.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository link and newly identifies Fairseq and one NVIDIA V100 GPU. It also documents the retrieval-skipping threshold. The detailed FAISS configuration, calibrator architecture, training schedule and hyperparameters largely match v1; relocating them does not constitute new disclosure.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantial positioning around mechanistic interpretability, induction heads, FFN memories and compression, including an Interpretable LMs related-work subsection. It also characterizes the approach as learnable replay memory. These changes go beyond the numerous bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around MoNIM. Experiments gain thematic subsections, and the former main-text Analysis section moves into an expanded Appendix C. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond renaming.

P2.justification: V2 changes the paper from one to two columns, replaces the selective-memorization example with a mechanistic architecture diagram, redraws the scalability plots and adds an AMT comparison curve. Numerous tables are reformatted or relocated, including model configurations and ablations; the dataset-statistics table also combines validation/test columns.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical assessment through additional compression comparisons, selection analyses, timing evidence and explicit limitations. However, its central new FFN-equivalence account introduces log-probability interpolation without reconciling it with v1's probability mixture or clarifying which formulation produced the retained results. Tables 8 and 16 also disagree on zero-shot QA accuracy. The useful additional evidence and unresolved methodological clarity problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
